result.summary: All 9 acceptance criteria independently re-verified against the real committed code, not asserted from ELIXIR-DEV's report. (1) Implementation matches design §1-7 exactly: mix.exs deps/0 gains {:wasmex, "~> 0.15.1"} appended after :lua per the design's placement note; mix.lock locks rustler/rustler_precompiled transitively with no redundant direct entry; .tool-versions gains exactly one 'rust 1.97.1' line; plugin_handler.ex's run_guest/2 implements the read-fixture -> start_link -> call_function -> GenServer.stop (on every path, via `with`) -> outcome-map algorithm verbatim, including executed_in_pid and the deliberately-longer wasmex-internal timeout vs. the outer PluginInterface.invoke timeout. (2) Read lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex in full (both old and new): the rust extension is additive only -- @recognised_tools gains "rust", parse/1 grows a third tuple element, report/4 and not_checked/4 thread running_rust through unchanged control flow, running_rust_version/0 uses System.cmd + rescue/catch (never raises, mirroring run/1's own outer guard discipline), F9 is documented in the moduledoc alongside F1-F8. Ran `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs` myself: all 30 pre-existing tests pass unmodified (the substring-based stdout/stderr assertions still match because the new '/ Rust ...' suffix is appended after the existing asserted substrings, not interleaved). (3) Read .github/workflows/ci.yml in full as YAML: the 'Read pinned Rust version' step's heredoc-free `run:` block correctly greps '^rust ' and appends 'version=<value>' to $GITHUB_OUTPUT; the consuming dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable step correctly references ${{ steps.rust_pin.outputs.version }} (step id 'rust_pin' matches); WASMEX_BUILD: true is scoped as env: under the 'Run backend gate' step only, not job-wide; step ordering places Rust setup after Elixir/OTP setup and before the deps cache/install steps, as the design requires. No YAML syntax defects found. (4) OQ-D1 resolution independently reproduced from scratch, not merely read: installed rust 1.97.1 via rustup in this sandbox (matches the pin exactly), ran `WASMEX_BUILD=true mix deps.compile wasmex --force` myself and observed the real cargo invocation ('Compiling crate wasmex in release mode (native/wasmex)', 'Copying .../target/release/libwasmex.so to priv/native/wasmex.so') -- this is a genuine from-source build, not wasmex's rustler_precompiled fetch path. The plugin_handler_test.exs AC7 assertions (Wasmex.Native's external_resource attributes naming native/wasmex/src/*.rs, :code.priv_dir(:wasmex)-relative native/wasmex.so existing on disk, :erlang.ports/0 unchanged before/after a guest call) are plausible and correctly interpreted given the real deps/wasmex/priv/native/wasmex.so (72MB, present) and deps/wasmex/native/wasmex/target/release build artifacts found on disk. (5) `git diff --stat main...feature/WF02-REQ165-20260828` confirms lib/letflow/engine/plugin_interface.ex is absent from the 16-file diff; read plugin_interface.ex in full and confirmed invoke/2,3's Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/Task.yield/Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) mechanism the design cites at lines 187-232 is exactly what ships, unmodified. No new supervisor, no new @callback, no new ExecutionContext field. (6) Read decision 0014 Decision (1)-(4) and Reasoning (a),(d),(f) in full: Decision (2)'s 'every guest invocation must cross a process boundary first ... never called inline' is satisfied (handle_node/1 only ever runs inside invoke/2,3's Task); Decision (4)'s Lua-before-WASM sequencing is not implicated by this diff; Reasoning (a)'s residual-native-crash-risk framing and (d)'s 'PluginInterface needs no contract change' claim are both restated verbatim in substance in plugin_handler.ex's moduledoc; Reasoning (f)'s naming of wasmex as 'Letflow's first native-code build dependency' is exactly the CI/toolchain-pin work this diff does. No conflict with decision 0005's pinning convention -- the design mirrors it via the same .tool-versions/setup-action/never-fails-advisory-task shape rather than inventing a second mechanism. (7) Moduledoc content matches design §7.1/7.2 verbatim in substance and reuses plugin_interface.ex's own disclosed-and-uncovered vocabulary ('a hard kill of the BEAM node itself, or System.halt/0' appears in both files identically). (8) Independently re-ran the FULL suite myself (not trusting the '2294 passed' report): `WASMEX_BUILD=true mix test` -> 'Result: 2294 passed (5 properties, 2289 tests), 3 excluded' -- identical count to ELIXIR-DEV's report, confirming no ripple effect from the mix.exs/CI/shared-Mix-task changes. (9) Independently ran `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` (clean, 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings) and `mix format --check-formatted` (exit 0, no diffs). Also ran `mix letflow.check_toolchain` directly: prints the expected OK line naming Elixir/OTP/Rust all matching the pin. Ran `mix letflow.lint_handoffs`: 0 new violations (25 pre-existing grandfathered, unrelated to this branch) -- same as ELIXIR-DEV reported. No idiom violations, no supervision-integrity concerns (guest execution stays inside the pre-existing, unmodified PluginTaskSupervisor-backed Task boundary; no new process/supervisor introduced), no scope creep (the handler is deliberately trivial, no WASM-02 ABI machinery built ahead of REQ-166, no speculative config.exs entry added, matching the design's own explicit anti-scope-creep notes in §1 and §3.3). One minor, non-blocking observation for future maintainers, not filed as an issue since it is purely informational and already flagged as an open question by the design itself: OQ-D2 (precompiled-target availability for ubuntu-latest) remains genuinely unconfirmed since CI hasn't run yet in this workflow -- that is CI's job to demonstrate, not this local sandbox's, and does not change any of the acceptance criteria above.
